subject: Field report: multi-variant fallback causing tail latency — action plan + temporary override
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@fiscaltech.com>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@fiscaltech.com>
Date: 2028-10-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Observed tail latency with multi-variant fallback — can we triage?

Team —

Quick note from the FiscalTech POC this morning: their production-like workload hit a sustained tail latency increase for a subset of requests when our routing picked the "variant-b-quant" fallback (~15% of traffic during a capacity dip). The buyer flagged errors and long tails around the same time the system auto-switched variants.

Attached: a short trace + the SLO chart Priya shared (trace-20281015-fiscaltech-req1234.json, slo-tailchart-20281015.png).

Ask: can Platform/Runtime look at the fallback heuristics and confirm whether this variant has a pathological performance profile under FiscalTech's sequence-length distribution? If we can't get an immediate fix, we need a temporary routing override to route their account away from variant-b-quant for the next 48h (will accept manual policy change).

Customer impact: Priya — they're seeing ~95th-99th percentile token latency spikes, not full outages, but enough to break internal timeouts. Alex is looping in engineering.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Platform confirms root cause and ETA for fix (actionable triage notes)
- If fix > 24h, we do a temporary routing policy override for the account
- Sales Eng to coordinate customer communication and mitigation window

Thanks—
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@fiscaltech.com>
Date: 2028-10-15T12:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed tail latency with multi-variant fallback — can we triage?

Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up and trace. I pulled the attached trace and a few more spans from our observability: the KV cache warmup and model swap during fallback line up with the tail. A few quick observations: 

- Variant-b-quant has a sparse-kernel path that currently falls back to a CPU-bound routine for very long sequences (>2048 tokens). FiscalTech's test corpuses include long documents and a mix of short prompts which seems to exacerbate warmup.
- The runtime’s cooldown to switch back to primary is currently 45s; during that window their requests are still routed to the slow variant if capacity is low.
- Telemetry shows repeated tiny retries from the client (timeout 3s -> retry) which amplifies load during the fallback window.

I added two attachments in the shared drive (linked in Jira) — a filtered trace and the SLO delta.

Immediate suggestion: If Platform can temporarily set a route hint for deal FT-2028-Q4-EXP-42 to prefer primary-quant and disable auto-fallback to variant-b-quant for 48h, we can observe whether things return to baseline. If we get programming-level changes, we should consider: shorter fallback cooldown and a warmup heuristic for variants (only accept variant if its last N samples meet latency threshold).

Happy to join a quick voice if helpful.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@fiscaltech.com>
Date: 2028-10-16T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed tail latency with multi-variant fallback — can we triage?

Thanks for the detail and traces. I'm Platform/Runtime on-call this week — quick triage notes below.

Root-candidate: variant-b-quant includes a fallback kernel path for certain sparse attention blocks which we ported from the research kernel. That path isn't yet fully optimized for GPU batching and falls back to a slower execution path when batch composition is heterogeneous. When the system routes a subset of traffic to variant-b-quant during capacity pressure, those requests can queue in ways that blow out the tail.

What I can do now (short-term mitigations):
- Apply a routing override that pins FiscalTech to primary-quant for 72h (we can revert earlier). This is low-risk; I'll coordinate the policy change and log it in JIRA-RT-8792.
- Shorten the fallback cooldown from 45s -> 15s in the autoscaler policy for variant families (requires a restart window, estimate 4h with ops).
- Add a per-account session affinity flag to avoid routing churn (quick config toggle, no code).

What needs product/roadmap work (medium-term):
- Kernel optimization for the sparse path (engineering story, will take multiple sprints).
- Add warmstart latency gating and a health-check probe for variant selectors (product + runtime change).

I need the following from Sales Eng to proceed with mitigation:
1) Explicit approval from FiscalTech to apply the 72h override (we'll note impact and reversion plan).
2) A target maintenance window if you want the fallback cooldown shortened (to avoid impact during heavy traffic).

I'll open a JIRA ticket and attach the traces; linking JIRA-RT-8792 here. Marking ETA: routing override within 2 hours after signoff; cooldown change ETA 4h after schedule confirmation.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff, Platform / Runtime

To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Observed tail latency with multi-variant fallback — can we triage?

Karthik — thanks, that sounds good and pragmatic. From the customer side: Priya confirms they're fine with the 72h override as long as we schedule it now and commit to hourly updates during the window. Alex will be monitoring internal dashboards; they want to avoid a maintenance window during their 10:00–16:00 ET business hours.

My asks for Platform:
- Please apply the 72h override now (non-business-hour safe for customer: we'll do it at 18:00 ET today).
- Start the cooldown change once we hit a low-traffic window (Marissa request: after 22:00 ET).

I'll send a short customer-facing note confirming the mitigation timeline and the revert plan. Also looping in our Solutions Monitoring slack channel for a watch.

Action owner list (so we have clear owners):
- Karthik: Apply routing override at 2028-10-16T22:00:00-04:00 (proposed) and log changes in JIRA-RT-8792.
- Logan: Provide updated traces once override is live and keep telem dashboard link shared.
- Sean: I will send the customer communication and collect signoff in HubSpot.

Marissa

Priya / Alex —

Confirming the plan and next steps from our end per earlier thread:

- Routing override: Platform will pin FiscalTech to primary-quant for an initial 72-hour window starting tonight at 22:00 ET. Karthik will log the change and we’ll share hourly telemetry snapshots.
- Short-term cooldown tweak: Platform will schedule a cooldown change (45s -> 15s) during your off hours; we will confirm the maintenance window 24hrs in advance.
- Visibility: Logan will push updated traces to the shared drive as we observe before/after metrics.
- Roadmap items: Product and Platform will open follow-ups for kernel optimization and warmstart gating; I’ll capture customer ask in the deal notes so product prioritization has concrete impact evidence.

Expect a short customer note from me in ~15 minutes with the live schedule and an explicit opt-in. Thanks for the quick cooperation.

—Sean
